editorNote: This issue follows the chronological 1982 series into the week beginning September 6, when the home-arcade shelf was crowded enough for Parker Brothers' Frogger translation to become the headline while computer stores kept selling practical software and falling memory prices.
morningLine: Frogger jumps from coin-op fame to the Atari VCS counter as Chicago reaches No. 1 and E.T. retakes the weekend box office.

lead.headline: Frogger Hops Onto the VCS Counter
lead.summary: Arcade Express' September 12 Hotseat treated Parker Brothers' Atari VCS Frogger as a serious home-arcade translation, praising its authentic coin-op feel and sophisticated play. For stores, the frog was more than a novelty: it showed third-party publishers could compete for the hottest VCS shelf space with arcade licenses of their own.
lead.confidence: Dated September 12, 1982 Arcade Express review; wording follows the preserved review summary and later bibliographic references

computerItems.label: Arcade desk
computerItems.headline: Pac-Man Still Sets the Earnings Pace
computerItems.summary: Trade retrospectives for 1982 still identify Pac-Man as the year's highest-grossing arcade game, even as newer names such as Zaxxon, Q*bert, Time Pilot, and Pitfall! fill the release calendar.

computerItems.headline: ColecoVision and Atari 5200 Crowd the Fall Conversation
computerItems.summary: The 1982 console field is no longer just VCS versus Intellivision; new machines and arcade licenses make comparison shopping more complicated.

computerItems.headline: Software Sells the Machine
computerItems.summary: VisiCalc, WordStar, dBASE II, SuperCalc, and The Home Accountant remain the kind of named packages clerks use to explain why a microcomputer belongs at home or in the office.

market.headline: Cartridges Turn Into a Brand Fight
market.summary: The week's retail signal is that recognizable arcade names are no longer locked to a single maker. Parker Brothers, Activision, Atari, and Coleco are all teaching shoppers to compare publishers as much as hardware.

bbsNote.summary: A 300-baud call is still a patient ritual, but hobbyists are trading tips on modems, CP/M disks, and which arcade conversions are worth the cartridge price.

curiosity.headline: The Frog as a Salesman
curiosity.summary: Frogger's home success matters because it turns a simple road-and-river character into a box that can move systems, cartridges, and magazine review space.
